sources.title: Independent selected-action ratio and surrogate arithmetic
sources.details: For positive p_old, exp(log p_new-log p_old)=p_new/p_old. Separately conditioned selected probabilities: .4/.2=2, .1/.2=.5, .3/.2=1.5. The dimensionless ratio times fixed reward-unit advantage .6 is 1.2; it is an objective term, not measured quality. A batch/action construction with two normalized rows verifies the sample axis. Recorded in inspection-ledger.md and executed bounded-cpu code.

sources.title: Actual unchanged original fence CPU run

claims.statement: old policy is the policy that collected the batch; ratio is new/old probability of the same selected card for the same context.
claims.scope: Ratio 1 refers to the unchanged selected probability, not the entire policy; old selected probabilities must be positive.

evidence.locator: Section 3 definition of r_t and equation 6, PDF p3; Algorithm 1 p5
evidence.supports: Same state/action likelihood divided by the collecting policy likelihood; sample under old policy then update.
Store sampled logp and compare current selected logp against it.

claims.statement: The independent selected probabilities .2→.4 and .2→.1 have ratios [2,.5]; the two entries need not sum to one.
claims.location: 13.12 original Python fence and following paragraph
claims.scope: Batch axis contains two different selections, not one complete two-action distribution; ratio is dimensionless.

evidence.locator: inspection-ledger.md: Independent arithmetic, axes and execution
evidence.supports: Explicit divisions and normalized (batch=2,action=2) rows with selected action gather.
Unmodified fence displays [2.0,0.5].
Independent normalized-row construction and selected-action ratios.

verification.expected: [2,0.5]; each full context distribution sums to one
verification.details: Two selected-action samples, each with its own unobserved complementary action; no mixing of batch and action axes.
verification.tolerance: 1e-12 float64; displayed original float32 ratio checked after round(value,4)

claims.statement: The original code uses natural log, elementwise exponentiation and detach to form a fixed-old probability ratio.
claims.scope: Arithmetic demonstration: original inputs do not require gradient, and there is no backward or optimizer call. Enabled-gradient variation separately checks detach.

evidence.locator: torch.log API: elementwise natural logarithm definition
evidence.supports: Natural-log semantics used by Tensor.log.
Exp of a log difference yields the ratio for positive inputs.

evidence.locator: Tensor.detach API: graph and storage contract
evidence.supports: Old log graph is disconnected; detach is not a storage copy.
Actual original fence completed on installed CPU PyTorch.
Gradient flows to new logp but not detached old logp.

verification.expected: Original output [2.0,0.5]; old gradient None; new sum-of-unclipped-term gradient [1.2,-0.2]
verification.observed: All observed; old gradient null, new [1.2,-0.20000000000000007]
verification.details: API coverage includes torch.tensor, Tensor.log/exp/detach/tolist and rounding in actual execution. Official docs are version 2.9; actual environment is 2.14.1+cpu.
verification.tolerance: 1e-12 float64; displayed original float32 ratio checked after round(value,4)

claims.statement: Detach prevents old log gradient, but historical values must actually be saved; recomputing the denominator from the new policy would remove the change.
claims.scope: Graph separation and historical persistence are distinct. The current fence log creates a separate result, and original training captures selected old values once per rollout.

evidence.supports: Disconnects graph but shares storage; cannot alone guarantee immutability.
Historical logp stored independently; not recomputed as current logp in denominator.
Captures old_selected with clone before the repeated epochs; current selected values recomputed per epoch.
Detached alias changes with live storage; historical clone remains unchanged.

claims.statement: Implementations often store log probabilities to handle very small probability values.
claims.scope: Log representation postpones probability underflow; it does not guarantee every log difference or exp is numerically safe.

evidence.supports: Actual implementation stores logp and exponentiates only the log difference.
Positive probabilities can be represented by their natural log.
Ratio can be computed directly from the difference of retained log values.
Retained log values -1000,-999 yield exp(1), whereas converting both to float64 probabilities first gives 0/0.

claims.statement: A fixed advantage .6 multiplied by ratio 2 gives the surrogate term 1.2, which is not a measured doubling of answer quality.
claims.scope: One selected-action surrogate term, in advantage/reward units; neither training nor quality evaluation occurs.

evidence.supports: The objective is the empirical mean of ratio times estimated advantage.
2*.6=1.2; dimensionless ratio does not by itself measure quality.
Independent product yields first term 1.2.

verification.details: Advantage .6 is fixed as in 13.11; no optimizer or measured quality comparison.
verification.tolerance: 1e-12 float64; displayed original float32 ratio checked after round(value,4)

claims.statement: old sampling policy is refreshed for a new collection round; reference can remain the posttraining starting policy throughout.

claims.scope: Roles in this chapter's fixed-reference, SFT-to-PPO setting; this is not a universal requirement for every posttraining algorithm.

evidence.supports: Reuse collected samples for K epochs, then theta_old←theta before another collection iteration.

evidence.supports: .3/.2=1.5 and .1/.2=.5; new/new=1 for both.
